description.value: This study examined OPRM1 genotype effects on alcohol-cue-related BOLD activation and ventral and dorsal striatal functional connectivity in alcohol-dependent individuals.

spans.text: The present study examines genetic variation in the A118G SNP (rs17799971) of the mu opioid receptor (OPRM1) gene as a moderator of neural responses to alcohol cues and of dorsal and ventral striatal functional connectivity during an alcohol taste cues task.

value: First, we hypothesized that these differences are driven by weakened frontal control over ventral striatal reward signals.
No differences in dorsal striatal connectivity were hypothesized, as this polymorphism has not been implicated in habitual drinking.

spans.text: First, we hypothesized that these differences are driven by weakened frontal control over ventral striatal reward signals. This would be predicted by weaker fronto-striatal connectivity in G-allele carriers.

value: OPRM1 genotype moderated activation within the Alcohol versus Water contrast such that G-allele carriers displayed greater activation within regions including the right insula, bilateral supramarginal gyri, left precuneus, right superior parietal lobule, right orbitofrontal cortex, and right angular gyrus associated with presentation of the alcohol cue.
These findings suggest that cue-induced activation of opioid receptor-rich neural regions, such as the insula and orbitofrontal cortex, is moderated by OPRM1 genotype.

The negative connectivity observed may reflect greater frontal recruitment for self-regulation among G-allele carriers.
